title: Plans in beads
description:
# Plans in beads — how it should be

Gate: confirmed by user, 2026-09-04

A plan is a durable, shared record of what a feature should be and how it
gets built. Today it is a directory of markdown files inside one git
worktree. It should instead live in the repository's beads database — the
same store that already holds the issue backlog — so that every worktree,
every agent, and the user see one plan, in one place, for as long as the
repository exists.

This file is deliberately blind to implementation cost.

## Why files in a worktree were not ideal

- A plan pinned to one branch is invisible from a sibling worktree until
  it is merged, so parallel agents cannot read each other's plans.
- The directory is disposable: once the work merges, the plan is a pile of
  history that nobody reopens, and HANDOFF.md had to be folded by hand.
- The file layout (`<date>-<NN>-<slug>/`) needed a serial counter that
  parallel worktrees could collide on.
- Decisions, status and handoff were four files that drifted from each
  other; the backlog was a fifth place.

## Use cases

### UC1 — draft a plan from any worktree, read it from any other

Actor: a coding agent (or the user) in worktree `web/`.
Situation: starting a feature; a sibling agent in `main/` is mid-way through
a related plan.
Intent: draft a plan and see the sibling's plan without switching branches.

Walkthrough:

1. The agent invokes ngplan. The skill creates one plan bead (title, labels,
   the plan's idea statement) with a single `bd create`.
2. The bead ID is the plan's address. Anything that refers to the plan —
   a handoff item, a sub-plan, a commit message — names that ID.
3. In `main/`, `bd list -t epic` (or the plan label) shows the new plan the
   same minute, with the same content, no fetch or merge needed.
4. Both agents append comments to their own plans; nothing conflicts
   because the store is one database, not two branches.

### UC2 — review a plan in a browser, diagrams rendered

Actor: the user.
Situation: an agent reports a plan is ready for the idea gate.
Intent: read the idea statement and its mermaid diagrams as rendered
documents, and read the decision thread in order.

Walkthrough:

1. The user opens `crabswarm preview` in the browser. Beside the registered
   directory roots there is a "plans & issues" root backed by the beads
   database.
2. Selecting the plan shows the idea statement, the plan body, status and
   acceptance criteria as rendered markdown with mermaid diagrams drawn
   inline, using the renderer the previewer already has for files.
3. The comment thread renders below as the decision log: each
   `Decision:` and `Discussion:` comment in order, with its author and time.
4. Children (steps, handoff items, sub-plans) are listed with their status.
5. Fallback without the browser: `bd show <id>` prints the same fields as
   text, which is enough for an agent that never opens a GUI.

### UC3 — the plan outlives its worktree

Actor: the user, months later.
Situation: a defect surfaces in code that came from a plan whose worktree
is long deleted.
Intent: find the plan and its decisions.

Walkthrough:

1. `bd search "<feature words>" --status all` finds the closed plan bead.
2. `bd show <id>` prints the idea, the plan and the decision comments;
   the close reason says what shipped.
3. Handoff items born from that plan are linked to it and still open or
   closed on their own merits.

### UC4 — handoff items are born in the backlog

Actor: an implementing agent.
Situation: while executing a plan step, an out-of-scope defect is found.
Intent: record it so it survives, without a fold step later.

Walkthrough:

1. The agent creates a backlog task bead with a `discovered-from`
   dependency on the plan bead, in one command.
2. The step bead it was found under gets a `Discussion:` comment naming
   the new item by ID.
3. There is no HANDOFF.md and no fold moment: the item is already in the
   durable backlog, linked to its origin.

### UC5 — the idea gate lives on the bead

Actor: the user and the planning agent.
Situation: the idea round is done.
Intent: confirm the gate once, and have every later session trust that
record rather than chat memory.

Walkthrough:

1. The agent asks the fixed gate question.
2. On "Yes", the agent records the confirmation on the plan bead itself,
   with the date, and a `Decision:` comment saying the gate passed.
3. Any later session reads the gate state from the bead. A substantive
   edit to the idea statement resets it.

### UC7 — steps are children, status is what the children say

Actor: an implementing agent, and the user checking progress.
Situation: the plan is gated and its steps are recorded.
Intent: work one step at a time and see progress without reading prose.

Walkthrough:

1. Each implementation step is a child task bead of the plan, ordered by
   `blocks` dependencies where one step needs another.
2. `bd ready` shows the steps whose blockers are closed; the agent claims
   the first, does it, and closes it with the verification as the reason.
3. `bd show <plan> --children` and the GUI's children list show what is
   done, in progress and blocked. The plan's own status notes stay a short
   narrative on top of that, never a duplicate checklist.

### UC6 — a sub-plan hangs under its master

Actor: a planning agent.
Situation: a plan outgrows one bead.
Intent: split it without losing the whole-scope owner.

Walkthrough:

1. The agent creates a child plan bead under the master.
2. `bd show <master> --children` lists the sub-plans; the GUI shows them
   as a tree.
3. Each sub-plan has its own gate, decisions and steps; the master's
   acceptance criteria still cover the whole scope.

## Lifecycle

```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> Drafted: bd create (idea + skeleton)
    Drafted --> Gated: user confirms idea gate
    Gated --> Planned: contracts and steps recorded
    Planned --> InProgress: first step starts
    InProgress --> InProgress: steps close, handoff items created
    InProgress --> Done: bd close with the completion summary
    Done --> [*]
    Drafted --> Drafted: idea edited (gate reset)
    Gated --> Drafted: idea edited (gate reset)
```

## Usability requirements

- **One command to create, one ID to name.** A plan is created with one
  `bd create`; everything else is `bd update`, `bd comment`, or a child
  `bd create`. The ID is the only handle anyone needs.
- **Findable by type and label.** Plans carry a dedicated type or label so
  `bd list` can show only plans, only open plans, or the plans a backlog
  item came from.
- **Rendered in the GUI, on beads' own terms.** The previewer shows a
  bead the way `bd` models it — title, type, status, labels, description,
  design, acceptance, notes, comments, children and dependencies — as
  rendered markdown with mermaid. Plans are ordinary beads to it; the
  plan convention is only a way of using those fields, so the GUI stays
  useful for the backlog too.
- **Readable without the GUI.** `bd show <id>` must present the idea, the
  plan, status, acceptance and the decision thread in a sensible order.
- **Steps are children.** Progress is read from child status, not from a
  hand-maintained checklist.
- **Diagrams are always valid by the end of a turn.** Whatever path a
  write took — `bd create`, `bd update`, `bd comment`, inline text, a
  file, an editor — a broken mermaid fence is caught before the agent's
  turn ends: the agent is told which bead, which field and what the
  parser said, and cannot finish until it is fixed. The check does not
  try to know what this turn touched; it simply looks at the open beads
  (or the most recently modified ones) every time, so nothing slips
  through because tracking missed it. The user never opens a plan with a
  diagram that does not draw.
- **Nothing is folded later.** Handoff items are backlog beads from the
  moment they are found.
- **The gate is on the record.** Gate state is a field on the bead, never a
  chat memory.
- **No new sync burden.** Whatever syncs the backlog off the machine syncs
  the plans too; the user runs it, the agent never does.

## Settled in the idea round (2026-09-04)

- Steps are child beads (UC7); status is derived from them.
- Existing plan directories stay as history; the user will order their
  migration once plans in beads are stable.
- The GUI is first-class in this plan and generic over beads; the ngplan
  skill and convention feed back into `ngicks/agents-package` afterwards.
- The mermaid guard is an end-of-turn sweep over open (or most recently
  modified) beads, not an interception of individual `bd` commands and
  not per-turn change tracking, so every write path is covered by one
  mechanism that needs no state.
design:
# Plans in beads

Move ngplan plans out of `doc/plan/<date>-<slug>/` and into the beads
database, one bead per plan with steps as child beads; guard mermaid in
bead text with an end-of-turn sweep; browse beads, rendered, in
`crabswarm preview` as a generic issue viewer: a GitHub-style list with a
search query and a detail page with a dependency neighbourhood.

Status: idea gate confirmed 2026-09-04. Contracts and steps below are
drafted with tentative defaults; open questions 5–11 decide them.

## Goal / success criteria

Derived from IDEA.md.

- A plan created from one worktree is readable from every other worktree
  without a git operation (UC1).
- The user can read any bead — plans and backlog items alike — in the
  browser with description, design, acceptance, notes, comments, children
  and dependencies rendered as markdown with mermaid (UC2), and as text via
  `bd show` (UC3).
- The same viewer offers a GitHub-style list — a search query, Open /
  Closed / Plans buttons — and, on the detail page, the issue's dependency
  neighbourhood drawn as a graph; plans are `is:plan` plus affordances
  every issue gets, never a separate view (D14, D18, D20).
- A handoff item is a backlog bead linked to the step that found it from
  creation (UC4).
- The idea gate state is stored on the plan bead (UC5).
- Sub-plans are children of their master (UC6); steps are child tasks and
  progress is read from them (UC7).
- A mermaid fence that does not parse, in any text field or comment of an
  open bead, blocks the agent's turn with the bead ID, field and parser
  message.

## Scope

- The field convention (D1) and its identification rules: type, labels,
  metadata keys.
- `crabswarm issues lint`: sweep issues through the `bd` CLI and validate
  mermaid fences; a Stop hook that runs it (D3, D10).
- Issue sources in the preview daemon (`bd where` discovery, `--root` /
  `--issue` on `crabswarm preview`), `IssuesService`, and the SPA's tab
  header with the list and detail views (D4, D6, D13, D14, D15, D20).
- Repository instructions (`.apm/instructions/base.instructions.md`)
  updated to the convention.
- A boundary bead for `ngicks/agents-package` (skill rewrite, hook
  packaging).
- Dogfood: re-author this plan as the first plan bead once steps 1–3 land.

## Non-goals

- Rewriting the ngplan skill itself (ships from `ngicks/agents-package`;
  feedback after the convention and GUI are tried here, D4).
- Migrating the 14 existing `doc/plan/` directories (D2; the user orders
  it later).
- Editing beads in the GUI; writes stay on `bd`. Composing comments,
  editing content from them and a viewable edit log are a later plan, a
  writable issue board (D22).
- A plan-specific GUI. The previewer renders beads generically; plans are
  beads that follow a convention (D4, D14): a `plan` saved filter, and
  affordances — epic progress, comment-prefix badges, metadata chips —
  that light up for any issue that has the data.
- New dependency types. bd's `blocks`, `parent-child`, `discovered-from`
  and `related` are what the graph draws; a new kind is a request to
  beads, not a crabswarm change (D14).
- A kanban board and a whole-source dependency graph view. Both were
  drawn in the mock and dropped from this plan (D20); they may return in
  a later plan. The detail page's neighbourhood graph stays.
- Replacing beads' sync; `bd dolt push` stays the user's job.
- Reading Dolt directly. All access goes through the `bd` CLI (D5).

## Context

- Backlog: 45 beads (42 open, 3 closed) migrated 2026-09-04 from the
  retired `doc/plan/issue/`. Database `.beads/embeddeddolt` at the
  repository root beside `.bare`, outside every worktree; `bd` resolves it
  from any worktree via the git common dir.
- Read paths verified 2026-09-04 with a throwaway ephemeral bead (deleted
  afterwards):
  - `bd show <id> --json --include-comments` returns `description`,
    `design`, `acceptance_criteria`, `notes`, `metadata`, `labels`,
    `comments[]` (`author`, `text`, `created_at`), status, type, counts.
    Empty fields are omitted from the JSON.
  - `bd list --json` returns the same text fields, labels and metadata,
    minus comments; `--parent <id>` filters children; `--limit` defaults
    to 50 (pass 0 for all). Corrected 2026-09-06 while implementing:
    `bd show --json` returns an array even for one id; `show` reports
    dependencies as issue records with `dependency_type`, `list` as edge
    records (`issue_id`, `depends_on_id`, `type`); a missing id is a
    prose `{"error": …}` on stdout with exit 1, not a stable code.
  - `bd export --all` streams every bead as JSONL with comments; ~1.1 s.
  - `bd sql` is **not supported in embedded mode**.
  - One `bd` invocation costs ~1.5 s (embedded Dolt startup). Three
    concurrent invocations succeed.
  - Metadata: `bd create --metadata '<json>'`, `bd update --set-metadata
    k=v` / `--unset-metadata k`.
- Beads defines no semantics for `design`, `notes`, `context`; only
  `acceptance` has tooling (`--validate`, `validation.on-close`).
- Edges for a graph: `bd export` carries only `dependency_count` /
  `dependent_count`; `bd dep list <id...> --json` takes many IDs and
  returns a flat array of dependency records in one call, and
  `bd graph --all --json` returns open issues grouped by connected
  component (each with its issues; shape of edges to be confirmed against
  a database that has some — this one has none yet). One batched
  `bd dep list` per source is the planned edge source.
- Community beads GUIs (bd-board, Bead Me Up Scotty, beads-ui, BeadSpec,
  Lista Beads) converge on list, kanban by status with epic swimlanes and
  progress, a dependency graph, and a detail page, all reading through
  `bd --json` — the shape D14 adopts.
- Preview daemon (`crabswarm/preview/`): filesystem roots via
  `ListRoots` / `AddRoot` / `RemoveRoot` / `GetTree` / `GetDocument` /
  `WatchEvents` in
  `api/schema/proto/ngicks/crabswarm/preview/v1/preview_service.proto`;
  Connect handler in `crabswarm/preview/httpapi/handler.go`; markdown
  rendered by `crabswarm/preview/render/render.go` (goldmark, mermaid in
  client render mode, no CDN script). SPA under `web/src/`
  (Preact, `@tanstack/preact-query`, `preact-iso` router), documents at
  `/r/{rootId}/{path...}`, `mermaid` 11.16.0 already bundled.
- Hooks: `crabswarm hook exec` templates in `.claude/settings.json`,
  deployed by apm from `ngicks/agents-package`; the repo's own `apm.yml`
  lists only remote dependencies. `hook exec` supports Stop: non-zero exit
  blocks with the output as reason; `blockDecision`/`context` available.
  `hk` 1.57 is installed; no `hk.pkl` in the repo.
- Tooling: `node`, `npx`, `pnpm` on PATH; `mmdc` not installed;
  `web/package.json` has no `jsdom`, `happy-dom` or `mermaid-cli`.
- Command layout: `cmd/crabswarm/commands/<a>_<b>.go` per verb, RunE
  calling into `crabswarm/<a>/`; the go-edit-cobra skill governs edits
  there.

## Approach

### Convention (D1)

| Plan artifact | Bead | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Plan | type `epic`, label `plan` | title = plan name |
| IDEA.md | `description` | idea statement, use cases, usability |
| `Gate:` line | metadata `idea_gate_passed` = `YYYY-MM-DD`; absent = not confirmed | Q7 |
| PLAN.md | `design` | goal, scope, context, approach, surface delta, testing, risks |
| Success criteria | `acceptance_criteria` | |
| STATUS narrative | `notes`, via `--append-notes` | progress itself is child status |
| Implementation step | child `task`, label `step`, `blocks` deps for order | `bd ready` drives execution |
| Sub-plan | child `epic`, label `plan` | own gate, own steps |
| Handoff item | `task` with `discovered-from:<step or plan id>` | born in the backlog |
| Decision | comment `Decision: ...` | append-only |
| Open question / discussion | comment `Discussion: ...` | |
| Plan done | `bd close --reason` | completion summary |

### Components

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    subgraph agent turn
        agent[ngplan agent] -->|bd create / update / comment| bdcli[bd CLI]
        agent -->|Stop| hook[hook exec → crabswarm issues lint]
    end
    bdcli --> db[(.beads embedded Dolt)]
    hook -->|bd list --json + bd show --json| bdcli
    hook -->|temp .md per field| lint[mermaid-lint CLI]
    hook -->|non-zero exit: id, field, message| agent
    subgraph preview daemon
        svc[IssuesService] -->|ListIssues / GetIssue| client[crabswarm/issues client]
        client -->|bd list --json / bd show --json| bdcli
        svc -->|render.go| html[HTML + client mermaid]
    end
    html --> spa["SPA /issues/:sourceId and /issues/:sourceId/:issueId"]
```

### Data path: `bd` CLI only (D5)

A `crabswarm/issues` package shells out to `bd` with `--json`, with the
working directory set to the caller's root so `bd` discovers the right
database. Rejected in D5: a Dolt Go driver (huge dependency, duplicates
beads' storage layer, and embedded mode may not allow a second opener);
`bd export` per request (whole-database read for one bead).

### Preview integration: an "issues" surface beside "roots" (D6, D13)

The previewer grows a second top-level surface. The SPA gets a tab header
at the top of the page switching between **Roots** (today's file browser)
and **Issues** (beads). URLs move with it: the file browser's `/r/{rootId}/…`
becomes `/roots/{rootId}/…` — a breaking change to bookmarked URLs, accepted
by the user — and issues live under `/issues/…`.

Issues have their own registry, **issue sources**, beside the root
registry (D13). `crabswarm preview [DIR]` registers DIR as a file root
*and* resolves DIR's beads database by running
`BD_JSON_ENVELOPE=1 bd where --json` in DIR; the `.beads` directory it
reports (`data.path`) becomes the source's identity, so every worktree of
one repository maps to the same source. `--root` registers only the
directory; `--issue` registers only the issues source; neither flag means
both. A directory where `bd where` fails (`no_beads_directory`) simply
registers no source, and `--issue` there is an error. `preview list`
shows both registries; `preview remove` accepts a root or a source.

In the API the issues surface is its own Connect service, `IssuesService`,
in a new proto package `ngicks.crabswarm.issues.v1`, with source
management and the two read RPCs. Rejected in D6: RPCs bolted onto
`PreviewService`; a synthetic root over `GetTree` / `GetDocument`.
Rejected in D13: keying issues by preview root (several worktrees would
show one database several times; a root is a directory, a source is a
repository).

re-derive these from generic data and drift from the generic page).

The neighbourhood is drawn with the `mermaid` already bundled in the

### Mermaid validation: the `mermaid-lint` CLI already used for files (D9)

`ngicks/agents-package` ships `hooks/markdown-mermaid-lint`, a PostToolUse
hook running `mermaid-lint <files>` on edited markdown; the CLI is the npm
package `mermaid-lint-cli` (0.53.1 here, installed through mise). It
parses every ```` ```mermaid ```` fence in a markdown file without a
browser, reports `file:line:col: parse error: …`, has `--format json`
(per-diagram `line`, `type`, `ok`, `error`) and exits 1 on any failure.
`crabswarm issues lint` writes each text field and comment of a swept bead
to a temp file named `<id>.<field>.md` / `<id>.comment-<n>.md`, runs one
`mermaid-lint --format json --quiet` over them, and maps findings back to
bead, field and line. No new dependency: the dev environment already
provides `mermaid-lint`. Rejected in D9: a node script over the bundled
`mermaid` (a second engine to keep in step with the file hook);
`@mermaid-js/mermaid-cli` (Chromium per developer).

### Sweep selection: all open issues (D10)

`crabswarm issues lint` reads `bd list --json` (open, in-progress and
blocked — bd's default), then `bd show --json --include-comments` per
issue whose text contains ```` ```mermaid ````. At 42 open issues that is
one list call plus a show call per issue with a fence — typically a
handful — so a few seconds per turn. `--limit N` sorts by `updated_at`
and takes the newest N instead, any status; `--all` includes closed
issues. Modified `.md` files in the worktree are not swept here: they are
the file hook's job (`hooks/markdown-mermaid-lint`, D11).

syntax = "proto3";
package ngicks.crabswarm.issues.v1;
import "google/protobuf/timestamp.proto";
import "ngicks/crabswarm/preview/v1/preview_service.proto"; // Heading

// IssuesService exposes registered beads databases ("issue sources").
service IssuesService {
  // ListSources returns the registered issue sources.
  rpc ListSources(ListSourcesRequest) returns (ListSourcesResponse);
  // AddSource resolves DIR's beads database with `bd where` and registers it.
  // Re-adding a directory of the same repository is idempotent. Fails with
  // NotFound when DIR has no beads database.
  rpc AddSource(AddSourceRequest) returns (AddSourceResponse);
  // RemoveSource drops a registered source.
  rpc RemoveSource(RemoveSourceRequest) returns (RemoveSourceResponse);
  // ListIssues lists a source's issues newest-updated first.
  rpc ListIssues(ListIssuesRequest) returns (ListIssuesResponse);
  // GetIssue returns one issue with every text field rendered to HTML, its
  // comments, children and dependencies.
  rpc GetIssue(GetIssueRequest) returns (GetIssueResponse);
  // ListDependencies returns every dependency edge among the given issues
  // (all issues of the source when issue_ids is empty), in one bd call.
  rpc ListDependencies(ListDependenciesRequest) returns (ListDependenciesResponse);
  // WatchIssues streams change notifications produced by the daemon's
  // per-source poll (D8).
  rpc WatchIssues(WatchIssuesRequest) returns (stream WatchIssuesResponse);
}

// Source is a registered beads database.
message Source {
  // ID is a stable identifier derived from the absolute .beads path.
  string id = 1;
  // BeadsPath is the absolute .beads directory (bd where: data.path).
  string beads_path = 2;
  // Prefix is the issue-ID prefix (bd where: data.prefix), used as the name.
  string prefix = 3;
  // Dir is the directory the source was registered from; bd runs there.
  string dir = 4;
}

message ListSourcesRequest {}
message ListSourcesResponse {
  repeated Source sources = 1;
}
message AddSourceRequest {
  // Dir is a directory inside the repository; may be relative.
  string dir = 1;
}
message AddSourceResponse {
  Source source = 1;
}
message RemoveSourceRequest {
  string source_id = 1;
}
message RemoveSourceResponse {}

enum IssueStatus {
  ISSUE_STATUS_UNSPECIFIED = 0;
  ISSUE_STATUS_OPEN = 1;
  ISSUE_STATUS_IN_PROGRESS = 2;
  ISSUE_STATUS_BLOCKED = 3;
  ISSUE_STATUS_CLOSED = 4;
  ISSUE_STATUS_DEFERRED = 5;      // bd's fifth status (added while implementing)
}

message IssueSummary {
  string id = 1;
  string title = 2;
  string issue_type = 3;          // bd's type string: task, epic, bug, ...
  IssueStatus status = 4;
  int32 priority = 5;
  repeated string labels = 6;
  string parent_id = 7;           // "" for top-level
  int32 comment_count = 8;
  int32 child_count = 9;
  google.protobuf.Timestamp created_at = 10;
  google.protobuf.Timestamp updated_at = 11;
  int32 child_closed_count = 12;  // for the epic progress affordance (D14)
  string metadata_json = 13;      // verbatim JSON object; "{}" when unset — chips in list and board
}

message RenderedField {
  string html = 1;                // rendered markdown fragment; "" when the field is empty
  repeated ngicks.crabswarm.preview.v1.Heading toc = 2;
}

message IssueComment {
  string id = 1;
  string author = 2;
  RenderedField text = 3;
  google.protobuf.Timestamp created_at = 4;
}

message IssueDependency {
  string id = 1;                  // the other issue
  string title = 2;
  string type = 3;                // blocks, parent-child, discovered-from, related
  // outgoing is true when this issue is the edge's from side (IssueEdge.from_id):
  // it depends on, is a child of, or was discovered from the other issue.
  // parent-child rows are omitted here; children and parent_id carry them.
  bool outgoing = 4;
}

message Issue {
  IssueSummary summary = 1;
  RenderedField description = 2;
  RenderedField design = 3;
  RenderedField acceptance_criteria = 4;
  RenderedField notes = 5;
  string metadata_json = 6;       // bd metadata, verbatim JSON object; "{}" when unset
  RenderedField close_reason = 7; // close reasons are markdown too (mock finding)
  repeated IssueComment comments = 8;
  repeated IssueSummary children = 9;
  repeated IssueDependency dependencies = 10;
}

message ListIssuesRequest {
  string source_id = 1;
  // Status filter; empty means open, in-progress and blocked (bd's default).
  repeated IssueStatus statuses = 2;
  // Label filter (all must match).
  repeated string labels = 3;
  // Only children of this issue.
  string parent_id = 4;
}

message ListIssuesResponse {
  repeated IssueSummary issues = 1;
}

message GetIssueRequest {
  string source_id = 1;
  string issue_id = 2;
}

message GetIssueResponse {
  Issue issue = 1;
}

message IssueEdge {
  string from_id = 1;             // the dependent / child / discoverer
  string to_id = 2;               // what it depends on / parent / origin
  string type = 3;                // blocks, parent-child, discovered-from, related
}

message ListDependenciesRequest {
  string source_id = 1;
  repeated string issue_ids = 2;  // empty: every issue of the source
}

message ListDependenciesResponse {
  repeated IssueEdge edges = 1;
}

message WatchIssuesRequest {}

// IssuesChanged signals that issues of a source were created, updated or
// closed since the previous poll; an empty issue_ids means "refetch all".
message IssuesChanged {
  string source_id = 1;
  repeated string issue_ids = 2;
}

// SourcesChanged signals that the source registry changed.
message SourcesChanged {}

message WatchIssuesResponse {
  oneof event {
    IssuesChanged issues_changed = 1;
    SourcesChanged sources_changed = 2;
  }
}

- Node: the parse script over the visuals reference's diagram catalogue.

## Risks

- `mermaid-lint` is a third-party parser, not mermaid itself; a fence it
  rejects but the browser draws (or the reverse) is possible. Same
  exposure as the existing file hook; keep the version pinned in mise.
- Moving `/r/…` to `/roots/…` breaks bookmarks and the `web/e2e` specs;
  accepted (D6), no redirect planned.
- `bd` latency (~1.5 s per call) makes the sweep and the GUI feel slow if
  called per issue; mitigated by listing once and showing only issues
  whose text contains a fence, and by the 10 s poll interval.
- The daemon-side poll costs one `bd` call per source every 10 s even
  with no viewer; acceptable for a dev machine, and it goes away with
  `bd events --follow`.
- A mermaid-drawn graph is static; a neighbourhood stays small (one
  issue and its direct relations), and an epic with many children draws
  wide; the viewport opens on the current issue and pans (D21). D15
  names the fallback (a layout library) if a whole-source graph returns.
- The `bd dep list --json` record shape is unverified on a database with
  edges; step 7 pins it with a fixture from a real dependency.
- The Stop hook runs on every turn, including turns that never touched
  beads; acceptable at seconds, revisit with `--limit` if it grows.
- Empty fields are omitted from `bd`'s JSON; decoding must treat absence
  as empty, not as error.
- `bd` output formats are not a stable API; pin the `bd` version in the
  dev environment and keep the fake `bd` fixtures in step with it.

title: Issues board reads from one bd queue
description:
The issues board of `crabswarm preview` should feel live and cheap: a change made anywhere shows up on its own within the poll window, and a refresh or a navigation answers in about a second, however many tabs are open.

## Use cases

### 1. Edit a bead in a shell, watch the board follow

A user (or an agent) runs `bd update`, `bd close` or `bd comment` in a terminal while the board is open in a browser.

- Nothing needs to be clicked. Within the poll window the list re-sorts, the badge changes, the detail page re-renders.
- The delay is one poll window plus about a second. It is never "poll window plus twenty seconds".

### 2. Open or refresh the detail page

A user opens `/issues/{sourceId}/{issueId}` or reloads it.

- The header, rendered fields, comments, children and the dependency table all appear within about a second of the request.
- The dependency table shows every edge that touches the issue, both directions, exactly as today.

### 3. Many readers, one database

Several tabs, a reload storm, or the poll tick landing while a page loads.

- The daemon never runs two `bd` processes against the same beads database at the same time. Calls that would overlap queue and run one after another, in arrival order.
- Two identical requests in flight at once (the same listing, the same `bd show`) share one `bd` run and both get its result.
- A request that is cancelled while it waits in the queue (the tab navigated away, the daemon shutting down) leaves the queue; no orphan `bd` process is spawned for it.
- Different sources are different databases and stay independent of each other.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant B1 as Browser tab 1
    participant B2 as Browser tab 2
    participant D as preview daemon
    participant bd as bd (one at a time per source)
    B1->>D: ListIssues
    B2->>D: ListDependencies
    D->>bd: bd list --json (one run, shared)
    bd-->>D: listing incl. edges
    D-->>B1: issues + child counts
    D-->>B2: edges derived from the listing
    B1->>D: GetIssue
    D->>bd: bd show --json (queued behind the listing)
    bd-->>D: issue
    D-->>B1: rendered issue
```

### 4. Switch surfaces while issue requests are in flight

A user clicks Roots (or any other tab) while the board is still loading.

- The new surface renders promptly. Requests already in flight for the old surface do not hold the new one back.
- Static files the browser asks for on its own (`/favicon.ico`, assets) never wait behind API calls.

### 5. One vertical scroller

A user scrolls the board or a detail page.

- Exactly one box scrolls vertically: the content column. The page itself (the window) never grows a scrollbar of its own, at any viewport width, on the list, the labels page, the detail page and the Roots surface.
- The tab header stays put at the top; the sidebar stays put at the left.

## Usability requirements

- The browser's per-origin connection budget is respected: two long-lived event streams plus a handful of short API calls must fit under it without starving unrelated requests.
- No new configuration is needed for the common case. The default poll window stays as it is.
- Freshness: a request always reflects the database as of that request. The daemon does not answer from an older snapshot to look faster.
- Failure experience stays as today: a failing `bd` run turns into the same error on the affected RPC, and the poll degrades the live feed instead of taking the daemon down.
- A `bd` run started from a shell while the daemon reads can still collide with the daemon's run. That collision is bd's own behavior and is out of the daemon's hands; it should be rare because the daemon's runs are few and short.
design:
One `bd list` per source serves every read that today spawns its own process; the remaining `bd` runs are deduplicated and queued so the embedded dolt lock is never contended by the daemon itself.

## Goal

A board refresh or a detail-page load costs at most one `bd list` and one `bd show` per source, run one after another, and answers in about a second.

## Scope

- `crabswarm/issues`: `Client`, `Poller`, `Service`, `Summary`, `Edge`.
- Go fixtures under `crabswarm/issues/testdata/` and Playwright fixtures under `web/e2e/fixtures/bd-data/`, re-recorded from the live database.

## Non-goals

- Changing the proto schema or the web client source. The RPCs keep their shapes.
- Making the poll interval configurable.
- Serving from a stale snapshot (stale-while-revalidate).
- bd's usage telemetry (turned off by the user, outside the repository).
- Running or managing a `dolt sql-server`.
- Lifting the browser's HTTP/1.1 connection cap in the daemon (h2c). TLS and HTTP/2 arrive with the reverse proxy the user is putting in front.

## Context

Measured on this repository's beads database, 62 issues, bd 1.2.2:

| bd command | wall time |
|---|---|
| `bd list --json` (all statuses) | 0.8s |
| `bd dep list` with all 62 ids | 18s |
| two concurrent `bd list` | 3.4s (serial would be 1.4s) |
| four staggered `bd list` | finish at 1.3s, 2.6s, 4.1s, 6.3s |
| ListDependencies RPC (whole source) | 21s to 23s |

Root causes:

1. `Service.ListDependencies` (`crabswarm/issues/service.go`) with no ids runs `bd list` to collect ids, then `bd dep list <every id>`. bd answers that with one query per id. The listing it already ran carries every edge: `bd list --json` reports a `dependencies` array per issue in the flat `issue_id` / `depends_on_id` / `type` shape, identical to `bd dep list`'s output (verified: 23 edges, same set).
2. Every read has its own `bd list`: `Service.ListIssues` runs two (filtered, then all-status for `childCounts`), `Service.GetIssue` runs one for the children, `Poller.poll` runs one every tick. Embedded dolt holds an exclusive journal lock per process; beads opens with `fail_on_journal_lock_timeout` and the driver retries the whole engine open under an exponential backoff (initial 500ms, multiplier 1.5, max 5s, no limit). Concurrent `bd` processes therefore serialize anyway, but pay the backoff sleep on every hop and are ordered unfairly.
3. The daemon speaks HTTP/1.1 only. Two of the browser's six per-origin connections are held by the event streams; the slow RPCs occupy the rest, and unrelated requests (`/favicon.ico`, the Roots surface) stall behind them. Making every RPC short is what fixes this in the daemon.

Files: `crabswarm/issues/client.go` (`Client.run`, `Client.List`, `Client.Dependencies`, `Client.Get`), `crabswarm/issues/poller.go` (`Poller.Run`, `Poller.poll`, `changedIDs`), `crabswarm/issues/service.go` (`Service.ListIssues`, `childCounts`, `GetIssue`, `ListDependencies`, `clientLocked`, `startPollerLocked`, `RemoveSource`), `crabswarm/issues/types.go` (`Summary`, `Edge`), `crabswarm/issues/fakebd_test.go` (the fake bd script), `web/e2e/fixtures/bd-data/` and `web/e2e/issues.spec.ts`.

Fixtures: `crabswarm/issues/testdata/list.json` and `web/e2e/fixtures/bd-data/list.json` have no `dependencies` arrays and key on `crabswarm-no2`, an issue that no longer exists. Both sets are re-recorded from the live database; tests and e2e expectations move to the recorded ids. Every recorded file states its producing command and bd version in a sibling `README.md`.

## Approach

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    subgraph RPCs
        LI[ListIssues]
        GI[GetIssue]
        LD[ListDependencies]
        T[poll tick]
    end
    R["Poller.Refresh (singleflight)"]
    LI --> R
    GI --> R
    LD --> R
    T --> R
    R --> D[diff vs baseline, emit IssuesChanged]
    R --> CR["Client.run: singleflight(args) over semaphore(1)"]
    GI --> CR
    CR --> BD[bd subprocess, one at a time per source]
```

- **Shared listing.** Each source gets its `Poller` when its `Client` is built, not when `Service.Run` starts, so RPCs work with or without the ticker. `Poller.Refresh` runs one all-status `bd list`, updates the diff baseline, emits IssuesChanged when primed and changed, and returns the summaries. `Run` calls `Refresh` on every tick. Concurrent `Refresh` calls collapse through a `singleflight.Group` inside the poller, so the diff and the emit happen once.
- **Derivation in Go.** `ListIssues` applies `ListFilter` to the shared listing: empty `Statuses` keeps everything but closed (bd's own default), `Labels` is all-of, `ParentID` matches `Summary.ParentID`, `SortByUpdated` orders by `UpdatedAt` descending with id as tiebreak, `Limit` caps. Child counts come from the same listing. `GetIssue` takes its children from the listing and keeps `bd show` for the text, comments and close reason. `ListDependencies` flattens `Summary.Dependencies` across the listing and, for an explicit id set, keeps only edges with both ends in the set. `Client.Dependencies` and `bd dep list` are removed.
- **Queue and dedupe.** `Client.run` keys a `singleflight.Group` on the joined argument list and, inside the flight, acquires a per-client `semaphore.Weighted` of weight 1 with the flight's context. Waiters that are cancelled return `ctx.Err()` without spawning anything. Flights run under `context.WithoutCancel` of the caller plus a fixed timeout, so a caller that disconnects does not abort a run other callers share.
- **Emit from RPC refreshes.** A refresh triggered by an RPC that sees a change emits IssuesChanged like a tick does. The browser then does one extra bounded refetch; the baseline and the event feed never disagree.

Rejected alternatives are recorded as `Decision:` comments on this epic.

## Public surface delta

No dependency change: `golang.org/x/sync` is already a direct requirement; `singleflight` and `semaphore` are subpackages of it. No proto change. No config, flag or route change.

```go
// crabswarm/issues/types.go

type Summary struct {
	// ... existing fields unchanged ...

	// Dependencies are the outgoing edges bd list reports for the issue:
	// what it depends on, whose child it is, what it was discovered from.
	Dependencies []Edge `json:"dependencies"`
}

// Edge gains the tags of the flat shape bd list --json prints.
type Edge struct {
	FromID string `json:"issue_id"`
	ToID   string `json:"depends_on_id"`
	Type   string `json:"type"`
}
```

```go
// crabswarm/issues/client.go

// removed:
// func (c *Client) Dependencies(ctx context.Context, ids []string) ([]Edge, error)
// type depRecord

// unchanged signatures; run now dedupes identical concurrent invocations and
// serializes all invocations of one Client:
func (c *Client) List(ctx context.Context, f ListFilter) ([]Summary, error)
func (c *Client) Get(ctx context.Context, id string) (*Issue, error)
```

```go
// crabswarm/issues/poller.go

// Refresh lists the source once, updates the change baseline, emits the
// changed ids when the baseline was primed, and returns the listing.
// Concurrent calls share one listing.
func (p *Poller) Refresh(ctx context.Context) ([]Summary, error)
```

```go
// crabswarm/issues/service.go

// issueReader shrinks to what the service still reads through a Client:
type issueReader interface {
	IssueLister
	Get(ctx context.Context, id string) (*Issue, error)
}
```

Fixtures (persistent test data, re-recorded from the live database with bd 1.2.2, provenance in a sibling `README.md`):

```text
crabswarm/issues/testdata/list.json            bd list --json --status open,in_progress,blocked,deferred,closed --limit 0
crabswarm/issues/testdata/list_changed.json    same, after one recorded edit
crabswarm/issues/testdata/dep_list.json        removed
crabswarm/issues/testdata/dep_list_single.json removed
crabswarm/issues/testdata/dep_not_found.json   removed
web/e2e/fixtures/bd-data/list.json             same command as the Go list.json
web/e2e/fixtures/bd-data/dep_list.json         removed
web/e2e/fixtures/bd-data/show_<id>.json        bd show --id=<id> --json --include-comments, per issue the spec opens
```

## Testing and verification

- Unit, against the fake bd (`fakebd_test.go`): N concurrent `List` calls record one invocation; a waiter cancelled while queued records none; the fake bd gains an env-gated exclusive-run check (`mkdir` lock, exit non-zero on overlap) so "never overlaps" is asserted, not assumed; `Poller.Refresh` emits once for concurrent callers and emits from an RPC-triggered refresh; `ListIssues` filters and sorts equal the previous bd-side results on the recorded fixtures; `ListDependencies` edges equal the recorded `bd list` arrays, filtered for an explicit set.
- Service: a detail-page-shaped burst (ListIssues, GetIssue, ListDependencies at once) records exactly one `list` and one `show`, and no `dep`.
- Playwright (`web/e2e/issues.spec.ts`): dependency table and list still render from the re-recorded fixtures.
- End to end: daemon with `CRABSWARM_LOG_LEVEL=debug` against this repository, browser detail page load and a tab switch; the log shows no `dep list`, non-overlapping bd timestamps, and the page answers in about a second.
- Repository grep for `dep list`, `Dependencies(` and `dep_list` after removal.

## Risks

- A listing-derived filter that differs from bd's own (label matching, default status set) changes what the board shows. Mitigation: the filter tests compare against the previously recorded bd-side results.
- `bd list --json` could stop reporting `dependencies` in a future bd. Mitigation: the fixture README records the version; the decode test fails loudly on an empty array where edges are expected.
- A detached, timed-out flight could keep a bd process alive after its callers left. Mitigation: the fixed timeout is short (tens of seconds) and logged.

- [ ] The detail page and the board answer in about a second locally (ListIssues, GetIssue and ListDependencies each under 2s when fired together).
- [ ] Switching to Roots while issue requests are in flight renders promptly; devtools shows no multi-second Stalled time on `/favicon.ico`.
- [ ] ListDependencies for the whole source returns the same edge set as `bd dep list` over every id did (checked once against the live database and recorded in the plan notes).
- [ ] ListIssues honors status, label and parent filters and the updated-first sort exactly as the bd-side flags did, proven by tests over the re-recorded fixtures.
- [ ] Concurrent identical List calls collapse to one bd invocation; a caller cancelled while queued spawns none (fake bd tests).
- [ ] An RPC-triggered refresh that sees a change emits IssuesChanged (test).
- [ ] `go test ./...` and the Playwright suite pass on the re-recorded fixtures; `grep -rn "dep list\|dep_list\|Dependencies("` over the repository finds no remnant outside history.

title: MCP bridge attends and reports on Claude and Codex
description:
## Idea

An agent session that runs under cmdman is a chat member for its whole life, on Claude Code and on Codex alike, and the state its harness reports is visible in cmdman's status column from the first turn to the last. Nothing in that chain depends on the order processes started in, on a daemon restart, or on a harness that hands its MCP subprocess a stripped environment.

## Use cases

### A Claude Code session under cmdman shows its state in cmdman

The operator runs `cmdman compose up` for a project whose compose file starts Claude Code replicas. Each replica's harness starts `crabswarm chat mcp` as an MCP subprocess.

1. The bridge attends the room before the first turn. Whether the daemon was already up, comes up later, or restarts mid-session, the bridge is a member within a few seconds of the daemon listening, with no action from the agent.
2. A replica that was recreated (same compose name and scale index, new cmdman id) takes over the name its predecessor held. The predecessor's command has exited, so it is not a member any more.
3. Every hook-driven `crabswarm chat report-state` lands: the operator sees `working`, `waiting`, `done` change in `cmdman tui` / `cmdman ls` as the turn progresses.
4. A message sent to the replica reaches its terminal as a nudge once it reports `done`.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant H as Harness (Claude / Codex)
    participant B as crabswarm chat mcp
    participant D as crabswarm serve
    participant C as cmdman
    H->>B: start (stdio)
    loop until attending, for the life of the session
        B->>D: Join(kind=agent)
        D->>C: inspect token (state must be running)
        D-->>B: member
    end
    H->>D: hook: report-state working
    D->>C: status set working token
    H->>D: hook: report-state done
    D->>C: status set done token
    Note over D,C: operator sees the state in cmdman
```

### A Codex session under cmdman gets the same bridge

The operator starts a Codex replica the same way. Codex spawns MCP servers with a fixed environment whitelist that drops `CMDMAN_CMD_ID` and `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR`.

1. Codex starts `crabswarm chat mcp` and the handshake succeeds. The bridge never exits during startup, whatever the environment holds; a bridge that cannot identify itself stays up and its tools say so.
2. The bridge finds its identity token and the daemon socket anyway, because the shipped `crabswarm-chat` package tells Codex which variables to forward.
3. From there the Codex replica behaves exactly as the Claude one: attends, reports state, gets nudged.

### The operator can see why when it does not work

When any link in the chain fails, the daemon and the bridge say so on stderr at warn level by default. "Nothing happened" is never the only symptom.

## Usability requirements

- No new steps for the common case: `apm install` of `crabswarm-chat` plus `crabswarm serve` running is the whole setup on both harnesses.
- A member that joined once stays a member until its command exits; the daemon notices an exited command within one liveness check and frees its name.
- Every join says what it is: `crabswarm chat join --kind agent|human` is required, and a join that declares no kind is refused with a message naming the flag. A stale `SessionStart` join hook from an old package therefore fails loudly instead of quietly demoting the session to a human that is never nudged.
- Hooks never join. The bridge is the only automatic join, and the package README tells the operator to remove any `crabswarm chat join` hook entry an older install left behind.
- Who is nudge-capable is visible: `chat members`, `chat admin list`, the MCP members resource and the TUI roster show each member's kind beside its state.
- Failure text names what was looked at: the token, the room, the socket path.
design:
## Summary

Make the MCP bridge keep its membership for the life of the session on Claude Code and Codex, make the daemon stop vouching for members whose cmdman command has exited, require every join to declare its kind, and show that kind wherever members are listed, so hook-driven state reports reach cmdman.

## Goal

Every use case in the description holds end to end, verified by e2e tests against the real binary and a stub cmdman, plus one manual run against a real Codex session and this Claude session.

## Scope

- Daemon liveness: `crabswarm/chat/resolver` reads cmdman's run state; a command that is not running is an unknown token.
- Member kind: proto `MemberKind`, required on `JoinRequest`, carried on `Member`, rendered by `chat members`, `chat admin list`, the MCP members resource and the TUI roster; `crabswarm chat join --kind agent|human` replaces `--agent`.
- Bridge membership: `crabswarm/chat/mcpserver` keeps trying to attend for the whole session and never dies at startup for want of a token.
- Codex environment: `apm-package/crabswarm-chat/apm.yml` forwards the variables the bridge needs; the socket default survives a missing `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR`.
- Logging: a warn-level stderr logger is the default when no logging flag or env is set.
- Tests and docs: e2e for each of the above; README section on removing stale join hooks; release note.

## Non-goals

- Codex idle detection (Codex has no `Notification` event); the daemon's ten-minute staleness fallback stays the answer.
- Admin-plane `WatchRoom` for the TUI.
- Upgrading an existing `human` member to `agent` on re-join: a flagless join is refused instead, and an old database is recreated (release note).
- A log file sink for the bridge (deferred issue).
- Fixing apm's `\n\n` path substitution in deployed Codex hook templates (separate issue).

## Context (findings, all verified on 2026-09-07)

**Live symptom on this host.** From a Claude Code session under cmdman, the bridge's join is refused with `joining room "/home/watage/gitrepo/github.com/ngicks/crabswarm" as "devenv/claude-2": name already taken in this team`. Every `report-state` therefore fails `Unauthenticated: token is not attending any room; join first` (`crabswarm/chat/service.go` `caller`), `hook exec` swallows it, and cmdman shows no status. Who holds `devenv/claude-2` could not be read from the sandbox (no admin identity there). Host-side check to run: `crabswarm chat admin list <room>` then `cmdman inspect <holder-token> --format '{{.State}}'`.

**Root cause 1: liveness ignores the command's run state.** `resolver.CmdmanCompose.Resolve` (`crabswarm/chat/resolver/cmdman.go`) runs `cmdman inspect <token> --format '{{json .Config}}'` and reads only `dir` and `labels`. cmdman keeps answering for an exited command until `cmdman rm`. Recorded with cmdman v0.0.24 (`--import-host-env=false -E PROBE=1` so the config is stable); the recording lands as `crabswarm/chat/resolver/testdata/cmdman-inspect-states.txt` with the producing command in its header:

```
# each line: <phase>: cmdman inspect NAME --format '{{.State}} exit={{deref .ExitCode}} {{json .Config}}'
created: created exit=<no value> {"argv":["true"],"dir":"/tmp/x","labels":{"cmdman.compose.command":"c","cmdman.compose.project":"p","cmdman.compose.scale-index":"1"},...}
running: running exit=<no value> {"argv":["sleep","30"],...,"labels":{...,"cmdman.compose.scale-index":"2"},...}
status set on running: exit=0
stopped: exited exit=-1 {...}
exited: exited exit=0 {...}
status set on exited: error: command "exited" has no running monitor: reported status lives only for the current run
removed: error: resolve command: no command found matching "exited"
```

So `checkLiveness` (`crabswarm/chat/service.go`) vouches for a dead replica, `reclaimName` never frees its name, and a recreated replica deriving the same `<command>-<scale-index>` name is refused forever. The e2e stub cmdman (`e2e/crabswarm/chat_test.go` `stubCmdmanScript`) must render the state for the daemon's new format string.

**Root cause 2: the bridge's join gives up after ~3 s and nothing re-joins.** `joinWithRetry` (`crabswarm/chat/mcpserver/mcpserver.go`) makes 5 attempts and exits; `ensureJoined` re-joins only on a tool call; `watchMembers` (`resources.go`) is the only infinite loop but waits on `watchWanted`, closed only by an MCP `resources/subscribe` Claude Code never sends. Hooks cannot heal it: `report-state` does not join. Making `watchMembers` unconditional flips `TestServer_WatchesNothingUntilSomethingSubscribes` (`resources_test.go`); the go-sdk's `ResourceUpdated` must be confirmed to send nothing to a session without a subscription.

**Root cause 3: the bridge dies before `initialize` under Codex.** `mcpserver.New` calls `cli.ResolveToken` and returns the error; `runChatMCP` exits 1 with nothing on stdout. Codex 0.153.4 spawns stdio servers with a fixed env whitelist. Codex's `McpServerTransportConfig::Stdio` carries `env` (static table) and `env_vars` (names inherited from Codex's own environment) per `codex-rs/config/src/mcp_types.rs`. apm 0.29.0 passes unknown keys of a self-defined MCP entry through to every target's rendered config, so `env_vars` also lands in Claude's `.mcp.json`; whether Claude Code tolerates the unknown key is unverified. `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` is stripped too, so `defaultSockPath` (`crabswarm/config.go`) must not fall back to `/tmp`.

**Root cause 4: a stale flagless join demotes the session.** `/root/.codex/hooks.json` on this host still carries a `SessionStart` hook running `crabswarm chat join` (no `--agent`). The installed package (`apm.lock.yaml` resolved_commit e46a266) declares no such hook, so apm's merge left an older package's entry in place and does not remove it. That join makes the member `KindHuman`; `Store.Join` is first-join-wins, so the bridge's later `agent=true` join changes nothing; `CmdmanStatusMirror.Set` publishes agents only, so every `report-state` is stored and never mirrored, and `notify.SendKeys` never nudges. This is a second, independent cause of "no status in cmdman" on Codex hosts and survives fixing the bridge.

**Silence.** `loggerfactory.BuildLogger` (`internal/loggerfactory/loggerfactory.go`) returns a discard handler unless `--log`/`--log-level` or `CRABSWARM_LOG_FORMAT`/`CRABSWARM_LOG_LEVEL` is set, so "giving up on attending", "room event feed ended", nudge declines and the Codex startup error all vanish by default.

**Existing coverage.** `e2e/crabswarm/chat_test.go` has `startChatBridge`, `TestChat_RecreatedReplicaRejoinsUnderTheSameName` (stub forgets the old token outright, never the exited case), `TestChat_MirrorsMemberStateOntoCmdmanStatus`, `TestChat_TwoBridgesOnOneTokenAttendOnce`. `crabswarm/chat/mcpserver/mcpserver_test.go` covers join failure degrading to erroring tools and re-attending after the daemon forgets the member. Nothing covers: bridge started before the daemon, daemon restarted under a live bridge, a member whose command exited, a bridge launched with no token, `env -i` launch as Codex does it, a join declaring no kind.

## Approach

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    subgraph harness [Harness]
        HK[hooks: report-state]
        MB[crabswarm chat mcp]
    end
    subgraph daemon [crabswarm serve]
        J[Service.Join requires kind]
        L[checkLiveness]
        R[resolver: inspect State + Config]
        M[CmdmanStatusMirror]
    end
    C[cmdman]
    MB -- "session-long join loop, kind=agent" --> J
    J --> L --> R --> C
    HK -- "report-state" --> M --> C
    MB -. "env_vars forwarded by Codex" .-> MB
```

| Area | Change | Absorbs issue |
| --- | --- | --- |
| liveness | resolver asks `{{.State}} {{json .Config}}`; any state but `running` is `ErrUnknownToken` | crabswarm-243, crabswarm-5s9, crabswarm-wkf (agent half) |
| kind | proto `MemberKind` on `JoinRequest` and `Member`; `Join` refuses unspecified; `--kind` required; kind rendered everywhere members are listed | crabswarm-yby (by refusal), crabswarm-5f7 (visibility half), crabswarm-32s (no flagless joiners remain), crabswarm-ei9 |
| bridge | token resolved in `ensureJoined`; join loop runs for the session with capped backoff; `watchMembers` starts unconditionally | crabswarm-xlc, crabswarm-9rf (code half) |
| codex env | `env_vars` in `apm.yml`; sock default derives `/run/user/<uid>` when `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` is unset | crabswarm-9rf (config half), crabswarm-o53, crabswarm-sxj |
| logging | warn-level text stderr logger when nothing enables logging | crabswarm-1p7 |
| docs | README host-cleanup section; release note | crabswarm-8f7 |

Rejected alternatives are in the `Decision:` comments: kind upgrade on re-join, hooks that join, apm's `env:` indirection, a `/proc` ancestry fallback, a bridge log file.

The resolver keeps its narrow `no command found` classification for "unknown"; a state other than `running` is a second, equally narrow "gone" verdict; a missing or unparseable state is a lookup failure (member kept), never a reap.

## Public surface delta

### Dependencies

No change to `go.mod`, `web/package.json` or `apm.yml` dependencies.

### Proto

`api/schema/proto/ngicks/crabswarm/chat/v1/chat_service.proto` (regenerate with `go generate ./api/...`):

```proto
// MemberKind says whether a member runs an agent harness whose terminal a
// nudge may be typed into, or is anything else and is inbox-only.
enum MemberKind {
  MEMBER_KIND_UNSPECIFIED = 0;
  MEMBER_KIND_AGENT = 1;
  MEMBER_KIND_HUMAN = 2;
}

message Member {
  string name = 1;
  string team = 2;
  string room = 3;
  HarnessState state = 4;
  // Kind is how the member joined. Unspecified only on a sender snapshot.
  MemberKind kind = 5;
}

message JoinRequest {
  string name = 1;
  reserved 2, 3, 4;  // 4 was `bool agent`
  // Kind is required; an unspecified kind is refused with InvalidArgument.
  MemberKind kind = 5;
}
```

`RegisterMemberRequest` is unchanged: an admin-registered member is always `MEMBER_KIND_HUMAN`.

### Go exported symbols

```go
// crabswarm/chat/cli/member.go
func (c *Client) Join(ctx context.Context, w io.Writer, token, name string, kind chatv1.MemberKind) error

// crabswarm/chat/cli/kind.go (new)
func MemberKindNames() []string                                   // "agent", "human"
func ParseMemberKind(s string) (chatv1.MemberKind, error)
func MemberKindName(k chatv1.MemberKind) string                   // "agent", "human", "unknown"

// crabswarm/chat/resolver/cmdman.go — signature unchanged, verdict widened:
// Resolve wraps ErrUnknownToken when cmdman reports the command in any state
// but "running"; the error text names the state.
func (p *CmdmanCompose) Resolve(ctx context.Context, token string) (TeamInfo, error)

// crabswarm/chat/mcpserver/mcpserver.go — signature unchanged, no longer
// fails on a missing token; the token is resolved on the first attend.
func New(logger *slog.Logger, sockPath, token string) (*Server, error)
```

### CLI

```console
crabswarm chat join --kind agent            # required; --agent is removed
crabswarm chat join --kind human --name me
crabswarm chat join                         # error: --kind is required: agent or human

crabswarm chat members
# devenv/claude-1  agent  working
# devenv/claude-2  agent  done
# admin/me         human  done
# first column unchanged: exactly the address `chat send` takes

crabswarm chat admin list
# <room>
#   <team>
#     <name>  agent  working        # kind added after the name
```

The MCP `chat_members` tool prints the same lines as `chat members`, and its description says the first column is the address. The MCP members resource gains `"kind": "agent"|"human"` per member. The TUI roster row (`crabswarm/chat/cli/tui/members.go`) shows the kind between the name and the state.

### Config and environment

`crabswarm/config.go` `defaultSockPath`: `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/crabswarm/default.sock`, else `/run/user/<uid>/crabswarm/default.sock` when that directory exists, else `/tmp/crabswarm/default.sock`.

Logging default (`internal/loggerfactory`): with no `--log`, `--log-level`, `CRABSWARM_LOG_FORMAT` or `CRABSWARM_LOG_LEVEL`, every `crabswarm` command logs warn and above as text to stderr. Any of those settings replaces the default as today.

### apm package

`apm-package/crabswarm-chat/apm.yml`:

```yaml
dependencies:
  mcp:
  - name: crabswarm-chat
    registry: false
    transport: stdio
    command: crabswarm
    args: [chat, mcp]
    env_vars: [CMDMAN_CMD_ID, CRABSWARM_CHAT_TOKEN, XDG_RUNTIME_DIR]
```

### Persistent data

No schema change: `members.kind` already exists. Old databases still recreate (release note, existing issue crabswarm-8f7).

## Testing and verification

- `crabswarm/chat/resolver`: table test over `testdata/cmdman-inspect-states.txt` — `running` resolves, `created`/`exited` are `ErrUnknownToken`, malformed output is a plain error.
- `crabswarm/chat`: `Join` with unspecified kind is `InvalidArgument`; `memberProto` carries kind.
- `crabswarm/chat/mcpserver`: tokenless `New` succeeds and tools report the missing identity; join loop keeps retrying past five attempts; `watchMembers` runs without a subscription and announces nothing to an unsubscribed session.
- `e2e/crabswarm`: exited command is reaped and its name reclaimed by a recreated replica; bridge started before the daemon attends once the daemon listens; daemon restarted under a live bridge re-attends and re-publishes state; `env -i HOME PATH` bridge answers `initialize`; `env -i` plus the three `env_vars` names joins; `chat join` without `--kind` fails with the flag named; members/admin list/TUI show the kind; package test asserts `env_vars` in `apm.yml`.
- Manual, recorded in notes: real Codex 0.153 session under cmdman joins and reports state; Claude Code tolerates `env_vars` in `.mcp.json`; this Claude session's `report-state` changes `cmdman ls`.

## Risks

- A cmdman whose `inspect` output changes shape would reap every agent at once; the resolver treats an unrecognised state string as a lookup failure and keeps the member.
- Unconditional `watchMembers` costs the daemon one stream per bridge.
- `env_vars` in `.mcp.json` may make Claude Code warn or refuse the server; if so, the `/proc` ancestry fallback becomes a follow-up.
- The warn-level default changes stderr of every command; `hook exec` captures stderr and its templates branch on stdout, so hooks are unaffected, but scripts that compare stderr will see new lines.

title: Native notify spike: Claude Channels
description:
Replace the chat notifier's brittle `send-keys` nudges for **Claude Code** with a crabswarm-owned **channel server** speaking the openly specified Claude Code Channels contract, so message-arrival events reach Claude agents through a documented protocol instead of typed keystrokes. Codex stays on `send-keys` by user decision (see the Track B decision comment). This is a **spike**: the deliverable is a working prototype plus a go/no-go recommendation, not production integration. ## How it should be ### Track A — crabswarm as a Claude Code channel server - A channel is an MCP server Claude Code spawns as a local subprocess over stdio; delivery never touches Anthropic infra. The contract is openly specified: declare `capabilities.experimental['claude/channel']`, emit `notifications/claude/channel`; reply tools and permission relay are also specced. Any language qualifies, so a Go binary works. Ref: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/channels-reference - crabswarm itself should be the channel server (working name `crabswarm chat channel-serve`): launched by Claude Code inside the devenv container, it dials the daemon over the already-mounted UDS, subscribes to arrival events for its member, and pushes them into the session. Ideally it also exposes a reply tool so the agent answers without shelling out. - This inverts the container-boundary problem of mounting endpoints out toward the host: the channel connects outward, nothing needs mounting toward the host. - Known preview blockers (why this is a spike, not a v1 adapter): channels require Anthropic auth (feature-flag gating of the research preview, not message routing), the `--channels` flag at launch, and a custom channel needs `--dangerously-load-development-channels` plus an interactive full-screen confirmation dialog on every launch, which is hostile to automated agent spawning. The org escape hatch (`allowedChannelPlugins`) exists only under Team/Enterprise managed settings. Flag syntax and contract "may change based on feedback." ### Track B — Codex app-server (out of scope, context only) Codex remains on the `send-keys` fallback. Preserved facts for whenever Codex-native notification is revisited: the Codex app-server protocol is JSON-RPC 2.0 over stdio with `thread/start|resume|fork`, `turn/start`, `turn/steer`, `thread/inject_items`; it controls only sessions it spawned (no attach to a separately running Codex TUI, openai/codex#25914), so using it would make crabswarm/cmdman own the Codex session lifecycle; and it is experimental and unsupported for production. Refs: https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/app-server , https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/codex-rs/app-server/README.md ```mermaid flowchart LR subgraph host["host"] daemon["crabswarm serve
(chat inboxes)"] end subgraph c1["devenv container (Claude Code)"] cc["claude --channels ..."] ch["crabswarm chat channel-serve
(MCP stdio subprocess)"] cc -- spawns / stdio --- ch end subgraph c2["devenv container (Codex)"] cx["codex TUI, stays on cmdman send-keys"] end ch -- "mounted UDS: subscribe" --> daemon daemon -. "send-keys via cmdman" .-> cx ``` ## Use cases ### UC1 — Claude agent gets a chat message while idle - **Actor:** a Claude Code agent session in a devenv container, a chat member via the join flow. - **Walkthrough:** a teammate sends it a message; the daemon marks the inbox; the channel server (subscribed over the mounted UDS) emits a `notifications/claude/channel` event; the idle session starts a turn, reads the event, runs `crabswarm chat read`, acts, and replies via the channel's reply tool or `chat send`. ### UC2 — Operator evaluates whether Channels can replace send-keys - **Actor:** the developer running this spike. - **Walkthrough:** launches a claude session with the dev flag plus the crabswarm channel; measures reliability against `send-keys` (idle wake, busy-turn queueing, transcript cleanliness); documents the launch friction (dialog, flags); delivers a go/no-go recommendation with the conditions under which chat should adopt it. ## Usability requirements - Zero per-message human interaction once a session is up. Launch-time friction (the dev-flag dialog) is acceptable for the spike but must be called out in the recommendation. - The channel server must fail soft: daemon unreachable means log and idle, never crash the agent session. - The spike's outcome must state, concretely, what the production adapter would look like: config keys, `JoinRequest` fields to un-reserve, launch wiring, degradation story.
design:
**Summary:** spike a crabswarm-owned Claude Code channel server as the official-protocol replacement for the chat notifier's `send-keys` nudges, ending in a go/no-go recommendation for the chat notifier.

> Skeleton until the idea gate passes. Resolve the open `Discussion:` comments with the user and run the gate before detailing the approach and steps.

## Goal / success criteria

- Working prototype: a Go MCP-stdio channel server that pushes a chat arrival event into a live Claude Code session launched with the dev flag. Codex is out of scope and stays on `send-keys`.
- A written recommendation: adopt / defer for Claude, with the exact adapter surface chat would need (config keys, `JoinRequest` fields 2–3 to un-reserve, launch wiring, degradation story).

## Scope (tentative)

- New spike code, location to be decided (suggestion: `crabswarm/chat/channel/`, or a branch-only prototype; see the deliverable-form discussion).
- No changes to the shipped chat surface; this plan only produces evidence and a recommendation.

## Non-goals

- Shipping a production adapter (promotion is a separate decision).
- OpenCode adapter (pending the opencode discussion; needs no spike, its HTTP API is documented).
- Solving the channels preview allowlist (Anthropic-side; friction is documented, not worked around beyond the dev flag).

## Context — verified facts to build on

Verified 2026-08-26/27; details and links in `doc/plan/2026-08-26-01-chat_subcommand/notification_mechanisms.md`.

- Channel contract (open, any language): MCP stdio subprocess; declare `capabilities.experimental['claude/channel']`; emit `notifications/claude/channel`; reply tools and permission relay specced. https://code.claude.com/docs/en/channels-reference
- Delivery is fully local; the Anthropic-auth requirement is preview feature-flag gating, not routing.
- Custom channels: `claude --dangerously-load-development-channels server:<name>` plus an interactive full-screen confirmation each launch; the org allowlist (`allowedChannelPlugins`) is Team/Enterprise-only.
- Codex app-server: JSON-RPC 2.0 stdio, powers the VS Code extension; no attach to foreign sessions (openai/codex#25914); experimental, unsupported for production.
- Seams reserved in the current tree for this spike:
  - `Notifier` interface in `crabswarm/chat/service.go` (the `send-keys` implementation lives in `crabswarm/chat/notify/`).
  - `JoinRequest` fields 2–3 are `reserved` in `api/schema/proto/ngicks/crabswarm/chat/v1/chat.proto` for self-reported native notify endpoints.
  - `chat.notify` config left empty.
- Since the plan was drafted, `crabswarm chat mcp` (`crabswarm/chat/mcpserver/`) already runs one MCP stdio bridge per agent, auto-joins on startup, and is wired by `apm-package/crabswarm-chat`. The spike's channel server overlaps that process model; see the existing-bridge discussion.

## Boundary ledger

| Deliverable | Owner |
| --- | --- |
| v1 send-keys notifier | shipped (`crabswarm/chat/notify/`) |
| Notifier interface seam | shipped (`crabswarm/chat/service.go`) |
| Claude channel-server prototype + go/no-go | **this plan** |
| Codex notification | stays cmdman `send-keys`; native path owned by nobody until revisited |
| OpenCode HTTP adapter | pending the opencode discussion |
| Promotion of any adapter into production | a later plan |
